correctness.rationale: Proof is self-contained: the exact Dirichlet–Neumann drifted resolvent solves D u″+a u′−r u=0, u(0)=1, u′(L)=0; its reflected-wall term is exponentially smaller for fixed interior x. The upper Skorokhod map is monotone when the driving input difference is nonnegative and nondecreasing; bounding the OU velocity path between its initial value ± its oscillation on [0,r^(−1/3)] sandwiches the discounted target-hitting probabilities. The truncation error e^(−r^(2/3)) is negligible relative to e^(−x sqrt(r/D)); OU path continuity and finite exponential moments enable dominated convergence. Independent full resets give the exact renewal identity (1−p)/(rp). Deterministic finite checks are reported separately, without claiming they prove the limit.

Neither the stationary MSD nor qualitative finite-rate phase shifts imply this coefficient. originality.rationale: The primary 2026 AOUP paper derives weak-activity first-passage approximations and numerically contrasts velocity redraw protocols; its reported results do not supply the exact fixed-activity r→∞ reset-velocity Laplace-moment factor. Linn–Lawley 2023 yields universal frequent-reset limits once the small-time absorption probability is known but does not calculate the OU-propulsion and reflecting-boundary prefactor. This result isolates and proves that missing coefficient; the generic renewal identity and constant-drift Brownian formula are prior tools, not claims of originality.
residual_risks: A general small-time diffusion heat-kernel or moving-boundary hitting theorem might imply the AOUP velocity prefactor after direct specialization; absence of direct matching searches cannot rule that out.
Published versions and all citations of the primary paper were not exhaustively independently reviewed.
The result is leading-order only; no quantified uniform error for all model parameters.

value.rationale: The explicit random-velocity prefactor resolves a central source-paper control choice: resampling stationary self-propulsion versus a prescribed velocity at every restart. It predicts a nontrivial, rate-independent multiplicative performance difference at strong resetting without weak-activity perturbation. The factor can be large for appreciable activity and target distance, so it is physically interpretable and experimentally testable; it is not an arbitrary arithmetic slice.
